quote: Theorem 6 (Likelihood ratio ordering in δ = α/θ). Let X1 ∼ LBD(λ, α1 , θ1 ) and X2 ∼ LBD(λ, α2 , θ2 ) be random variables with common scale parameter λ > 0, and let δi = αi /θi for i = 1, 2. If δ1 < δ2 , then X2 ≤lr X1 , and consequently, X2 ≤hr X1 and X2 ≤st X1 .
family: Lomax–Bilal distribution LBD(λ,α,θ) within the Bilal-G (T-X) family; density depends on α,θ only via δ = α/θ
compared: two LBD variables differing in δ = α/θ (same λ)

hypotheses.text: δ1 < δ2 (i.e., α1/θ1 < α2/θ2), common λ > 0

conclusion.direction: X2 <=lr X1 (g(·;δ2)/g(·;δ1) decreasing), hence X2 <=hr X1 and X2 <=st X1

ambiguity: Monotonicity of ψ(x) = (1−u^δ1)/(1−u^δ2) argued via boundary behavior rather than a global derivative.

quote: Theorem 7 (Likelihood ratio ordering in λ). Let X1 ∼ LBD(λ1 , α, θ ) and X2 ∼ LBD(λ2 , α, θ ) be random variables with common shape ratio δ = α/θ. If λ1 < λ2 , then X1 ≤lr X2 , and consequently, X1 ≤hr X2 and X1 ≤st X2 .
family: Lomax–Bilal distribution LBD(λ,α,θ); common α, θ (δ = α/θ)
compared: two LBD variables differing in scale λ

conclusion.direction: X1 <=lr X2 (g(·;λ1)/g(·;λ2) decreasing), hence X1 <=hr X2 and X1 <=st X2

ambiguity: Monotonicity of ϕ(x) = (1−u1^δ)/(1−u2^δ) argued via boundary limits λ2/λ1 → 1 rather than a global derivative.
